# WARNING: Install these libraries before running this code.
We're using the *nhanesA* package instead of regular NHANES so that we can create an aggregate dataset that has more datapoints.

```{r Install Packages}
install.packages(c("dplyr", "nhanesA", "leaps"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

## Raw Data Collection by Downloading from NHANES directly
We divide by three for the final line because each NHANES sample collects information from 300 million people.\\
Without dividing by three, it's equivalent to treating the dataset as sampling from 900 million people.\\

Note: we are specifically using the cycles from 2011 - 2016 because:\\
- Race encoding for Non-Hispanic Asian *(from 2011 onwards)*
- Alcohol consumption encoding was changed from 2017-2018 and onwards

```{r Create raw data table}

library(dplyr)
library(nhanesA)

cycles <- c("2011-2012" = "_G", "2013-2014" = "_H", "2015-2016" = "_I")

tables <- list(
  DEMO = c("RIDAGEYR", "RIAGENDR", "RIDRETH3", "DMDEDUC2", "DMDEDUC3",
           "SDMVPSU", "SDMVSTRA", "WTINT2YR", "WTMEC2YR"),
  BPX  = paste0("BPXSY", 1:4),
  BMX  = "BMXBMI",
  SLQ  = c("SLD010H", "SLD012"),
  PAQ  = c("PAQ650", "PAQ665", "PAQ710", "PAQ715"),
  ALQ  = c("ALQ101", "ALQ110", "ALQ120Q", "ALQ120U", "ALQ130"),
  SMQ  = c("SMQ020", "SMQ040"),
  DUQ  = c("DUQ200", "DUQ211"),
  BPQ  = c("BPQ020", "BPQ040A", "BPQ050A"),
  DXX  = "DXDTOPF",
  INQ  = "IND235"
)

pieces <- list()
for (cyc in names(cycles)) {
  sfx    <- cycles[[cyc]]
  merged <- NULL
  for (tbl in names(tables)) {
    d <- nhanes(paste0(tbl, sfx), translated = FALSE)
    d <- select(d, SEQN, any_of(tables[[tbl]]))
    merged <- if (is.null(merged)) d else left_join(merged, d, by = "SEQN")
  }
  pieces[[cyc]] <- merged
}

# See write-up above to see why we divide by three
CDCdata <- mutate(bind_rows(pieces, .id = "Cycle"), WTMEC6YR = WTMEC2YR / 3)
```

### Optional: Export raw data to CSV

```{r Export CDCdata}
write.csv(CDCdata, "raw_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Re-encode arbitrary internal labels to intuitive names

```{r Label re-encoding}
decoded_data <- CDCdata %>%
  mutate(
    Age  = RIDAGEYR,                       
    
    Sex  = factor(case_when(RIAGENDR == 1 ~ "Male",
                            RIAGENDR == 2 ~ "Female")),
    
    Race3 = factor(case_when(RIDRETH3 %in% 1:2 ~ "Hispanic",
                             RIDRETH3 == 3     ~ "White",
                             RIDRETH3 == 4     ~ "Black",
                             RIDRETH3 == 6     ~ "Asian",
                             RIDRETH3 == 7     ~ "Other"),
                   levels = c("White", "Hispanic", "Black", "Asian", "Other")),  # White = baseline
    
    CompletedCollege = factor(case_when(
                              DMDEDUC2 == 5                    ~ 1,   # college grad or above
                              DMDEDUC2 %in% 1:4                ~ 0,
                              DMDEDUC3 %in% c(0:15, 55, 66)    ~ 0,   # N/A: ages 18-19
                              )),
    
    BPSysAve = rowMeans(pick(starts_with("BPXSY")), na.rm = TRUE),
    BPSysAve = if_else(is.nan(BPSysAve), NA_real_, BPSysAve),
    
    BMI = BMXBMI,
    
    SleepHrsNight = coalesce(SLD010H, SLD012),
    SleepHrsNight = if_else(SleepHrsNight > 24, NA_real_, SleepHrsNight),
    
    PhysActive = factor(case_when(PAQ650 == 1 | PAQ665 == 1 ~ 1,   # Yes
                                  PAQ650 == 2 & PAQ665 == 2 ~ 0)), # No
    
    AlcoholYear = case_when(ALQ120Q == 0  ~ 0,            # Drank for zero days
                            ALQ120Q > 365 ~ NA_real_,     # Codes 777/999: refused/don't know
                            ALQ120U == 1  ~ ALQ120Q * 52, # Answered in terms of per week
                            ALQ120U == 2  ~ ALQ120Q * 12, # Answered in terms of per month
                            ALQ120U == 3  ~ ALQ120Q,      # Answered in terms of per year
                            is.na(ALQ120Q) & ALQ110 == 2 ~ 0), # Abstinent
    
    SmokeNow = factor(case_when(SMQ020 == 2     ~ 0, # N/A: never smoked 100 cigarettess
                                SMQ040 %in% 1:2 ~ 1,
                                SMQ040 == 3     ~ 0)),
  )

filtered_data <-  decoded_data |> select(SEQN, Cycle, SDMVPSU, SDMVSTRA, WTMEC6YR, # keep weight for re-sampling
                                  BPSysAve, Age, Sex, Race3, BMI, SleepHrsNight, PhysActive,
                                  AlcoholYear, SmokeNow, CompletedCollege)

# Filter for adults only, remove people listed as 80 years old because "80" in NHANES gives all people who are 80 or above, making it impossible to know their real age. Remove people whose BPSysAve is 180 or greater, because according to Mayo Clinic (who will be cited in the report), a blood pressure above 180 is indicative of an emergancy hypertensive crisis. This is not a normal reading someone would just get in a routine checkup, so these datapoints are either mistakes or at the very least not indicative or a normal situation. Also I restricted BMI to be less than 65, because apparently values greater than that are exceptionally rare and also not indicative of the general population.

filtered_data <- filter(filtered_data, WTMEC6YR > 0, Age >= 18 & Age < 80, BPSysAve <= 180, BMI < 65)
```

## Re-sample according to weights, to account for biases within NHANES

```{r Re-sample for weights}
# makes the re-sample reproducible
set.seed(1)

copy <- sample(nrow(filtered_data), size = nrow(filtered_data), replace = TRUE, prob = filtered_data$WTMEC6YR)

# drop the weights now since we're already re-weighted
pop_like <- filtered_data[copy, ] |> select(-SDMVPSU, -SDMVSTRA, -WTMEC6YR, -Cycle)

cleaned_data <- na.omit(pop_like)
```

## Output cleaned data to CSV

```{r Output CSV}
write.csv(CDCdata, "cleaned_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Check Interaction Term

```{r}
male <- cleaned_data[cleaned_data$Sex == 'Male', ]
female <- cleaned_data[cleaned_data$Sex == 'Female', ]

plot(cleaned_data$BPSysAve ~ cleaned_data$Age, xlab="Age (Yr)", ylab="Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)", main='Systolic Blood Pressure vs Age for Men and Women', type="n")
points(male$BPSysAve ~ male$Age, col=adjustcolor("blue", alpha.f = 0.01), pch = 19)
points(female$BPSysAve ~ female$Age, col=adjustcolor("pink", alpha.f = 0.05), pch = 19)
lines(lowess(male$BPSysAve ~ male$Age), col="blue")
lines(lowess(female$BPSysAve ~ female$Age), col="red")

legend("topleft", 
       legend = c("Men", "Women"), 
       col = c(adjustcolor("blue", alpha.f = 0.5), adjustcolor("red", alpha.f = 0.5)), 
       pch = 19, 
       bty = "n")
```






## Linear Model 

```{r}
model <- lm(BPSysAve ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + BMI + PhysActive + AlcoholYear + SmokeNow + SleepHrsNight + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data=cleaned_data)

summary(model)
```
# Fitting the linear model

```{r}
plot(fitted(model), cleaned_data$BPSysAve, xlab = 'Estimated Diastolic BP Values (mmHg)', ylab = 'Observed Diastolic BP Values (mmHg)', 
     main = "Actual vs. Estimated Diastolic Blood Pressure Values", pch = 16, col='blue')
abline(a=0, b=1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Residual Vs Fitted
plot(fitted(model), resid(model), main="Residuals vs Estimated Systolic Blood Pressure Readings", xlab='Estimated Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)', ylab='Residuals')

# QQplot
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
qqnorm(resid(model))
qqline(resid(model))
```

## Assumption Checkin

```{r}

# use this command to plot these in a single grid
par(mfrow=c(3,3))
# Residual vs each quantitative predictor
y_value = resid(model)
plot(x = cleaned_data$Age, y = y_value, main="Residuals vs Age", cex.main = 2, cex.lab = 1.5,
xlab="Age (Yr)", ylab="Residuals")
plot(x = cleaned_data$BMI, y = y_value, main="Residuals vs BMI", cex.main = 2, cex.lab = 1.5,

xlab="Average Nightly (Hrs)", ylab="Residuals")
```

```{r}
library(car)

### Run boxCox on the model in order to attain the optimal transformation for the response.

boxCox(model)

### This is how we find the exact suggested power transformation from boxCox.
which.max(boxCox(model)$y)
boxCox(model)$x[38]

# Transform the model.
transBP <- (cleaned_data$BPSysAve)^(-0.5)

lnAlcohol <- log(cleaned_data$AlcoholYear)

for (i in 1:length(lnAlcohol)) {
  if (lnAlcohol[i] == -Inf) {
    lnAlcohol[i] <- 0
  }
}

lnBMI <- log(cleaned_data$BMI)

trans_model <- lm(transBP ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + lnBMI + SleepHrsNight + PhysActive + lnAlcohol + SmokeNow + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data=cleaned_data)



plot(fitted(trans_model), transBP, xlab = 'Estimated RBI Values', ylab = 'Observed Diastolic Blood Pressue Values', 
     main = "Actual vs. Estimated Diastolic Blood Pressure Values", pch = 16, col='blue')


plot(fitted(trans_model), resid(trans_model))

qqnorm(resid(trans_model))
qqline(resid(trans_model))

summary(trans_model)







```

```{r}
# Justification for log transformations on BMI and AlcoholYear

# Evidently this is right skewed, log transformations solve this problem.
hist(cleaned_data$BMI)

# As can be seen here:
hist(lnBMI)

# This is also right skewed, apply a log.
hist(cleaned_data$AlcoholYear)

hist(lnAlcohol)







```

```{r}
library(MASS)
# Run "goodness" tests on transformed model with all predictors.

# Return reduced R^2
summary(trans_model)$adj.r.squared

# Return AIC
extractAIC(trans_model, k=2)[2]

# Return BIC
extractAIC(trans_model, k=log(nrow(cleaned_data)))[2]
```

```{r}
# BACKWARD SELECTION

# Run the stepAIC function in order to find the optimal model.
stepAIC(lm(transBP ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + lnBMI + SleepHrsNight + PhysActive + lnAlcohol + SmokeNow + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data=cleaned_data), 
        scope=list(lower=lm(transBP ~ 1, data=cleaned_data)), 
        direction = "backward", k=2)

# Fit the model using the suggested predictors from stepAIC. 
backwardmodel <- lm(transBP ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + lnBMI + lnAlcohol + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data = cleaned_data)

# Make plots
plot(fitted(backwardmodel), transBP, xlab = 'Estimated RBI Values', ylab = 'Observed Diastolic Blood Pressue Values', 
     main = "Actual vs. Estimated Diastolic Blood Pressure Values", pch = 16, col='blue')


plot(fitted(backwardmodel), resid(backwardmodel))

qqnorm(resid(backwardmodel))
qqline(resid(backwardmodel))

summary(backwardmodel)

# Compare "goodness" metrics.

# Return reduced R^2
summary(backwardmodel)$adj.r.squared

# Return AIC
extractAIC(backwardmodel, k=2)[2]

# Return BIC
extractAIC(backwardmodel, k=log(nrow(cleaned_data)))[2]


```




```{r}
# FORWARD SELECTION (Gives the same model as backwards selection)

stepAIC(lm(transBP ~ 1, data=cleaned_data), 
        scope=list(upper=lm(transBP ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + lnBMI + SleepHrsNight + PhysActive + lnAlcohol + SmokeNow + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data=cleaned_data)), 
        direction = "forward", k=2)

forwardmodel = lm(transBP ~ Age + lnBMI + Sex + Race3 + lnAlcohol + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data = cleaned_data)

plot(fitted(backwardmodel), transBP, xlab = 'Estimated RBI Values', ylab = 'Observed Diastolic Blood Pressue Values', 
     main = "Actual vs. Estimated Diastolic Blood Pressure Values", pch = 16, col='blue')


plot(fitted(backwardmodel), resid(backwardmodel))

qqnorm(resid(backwardmodel))
qqline(resid(backwardmodel))

summary(backwardmodel)


# Return reduced R^2
summary(forwardmodel)$adj.r.squared

# Return AIC
extractAIC(forwardmodel, k=2)[2]

# Return BIC
extractAIC(forwardmodel, k=log(nrow(cleaned_data)))[2]




```


```{r}

# This isn't too important, just ran a quick test of the best possible model with every number of predictors, the above model from forward/backward selection
# is still the best model.

library(leaps)

# runs all possible subsets
best <- regsubsets(transBP ~ Age + Sex + Race3 + lnBMI + SleepHrsNight + PhysActive + lnAlcohol + SmokeNow + CompletedCollege + Age:Sex, data=cleaned_data, nbest=1, nvmax=9)
summary(best)
```
